Passive acoustic monitoring of the Common Pauraque in the Pantanal

Source: R/data.R
curiango.Rd

Detections of the Common Pauraque (Nyctidromus albicollis) by two automated classifiers in one-minute recordings made at seven sites in the Pantanal wetlands and adjacent Cerrado, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, between November 2023 and February 2025, with an independent set of recordings annotated by ear. The occupancy unit is the site-night, the occasion is the one-minute recording, and the annotated recordings are the verified method of the multiple-methods design.

Usage

curiango

Format

A list with three data frames:

minutes

One row per one-minute recording (97,806 rows): site_night (site-night identifier, the occupancy unit), site (recorder site, one of seven), time (start of the recording), conf_custom and conf_birdnet (confidence scores of a custom-trained classifier and of the BirdNET global model v2.4, 0 when the classifier returned nothing), and the acoustic indices bio (Bioacoustic Index) and aci (Acoustic Complexity Index).

nights

One row per site-night (1,753 rows): site_night, site, night (date of the evening), and the nightly means of temperature (temp, °C) and relative humidity (rh, %), and the fraction of the lunar disc illuminated (moon).

verified

One row per annotated recording (1,199 rows): site_night, site, time, and y, 1 if any 3-s segment of the recording held the species.

Source

Piatti, L., de Sousa, D. L. H., Oliveira, B. S., de Melo, A. V., Sugai, L. S. M., & Provete, D. B. (2026). Data and code for: Methodological choices influence ecological inference in passive acoustic monitoring of a Neotropical nightjar. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.21795898 . Licence CC BY 4.0.

Details

The annotated recordings are an independent ground-truth test set of about 1% of the recordings, chosen in proportion to the number of recordings at each site, and annotated without reference to the classifiers (Piatti et al., 2026). They can therefore serve as the verified method of fp_data(). A detection by a classifier is a confidence score at or above a threshold; Piatti et al. (2026) used 0.40 (custom) and 0.10 (BirdNET) to maximize F1, and 0.95 for both to maximize precision.

The source table has one to 20 rows (detection windows) per recording, and a classifier's score is non-zero only in the windows where it detected the species. This dataset keeps one row per recording, with the maximum score over its windows, so a recording is a detection when any of its windows reaches the threshold. The script that builds it from the public deposit is data-raw/curiango.R in the package repository.

References

Piatti, L., de Sousa, D. L. H., Oliveira, B. S., de Melo, A. V., Sugai, L. S. M., & Provete, D. B. (2026). Methodological choices influence ecological inference in passive acoustic monitoring of a Neotropical nightjar. Journal of Avian Biology, in press.

Examples

str(curiango, max.level = 1)
#> List of 3
#>  $ minutes :'data.frame':	97806 obs. of  7 variables:
#>  $ nights  :'data.frame':	1753 obs. of  6 variables:
#>  $ verified:'data.frame':	1199 obs. of  4 variables:

# detections by the custom classifier at the MaxF1 threshold
mean(curiango$minutes$conf_custom >= 0.40)
#> [1] 0.01795391
